html:
Knud Rasmussen was a Greenlandic and Danish explorer, born in Ilulissat in 1879 to a Danish father and a mother of Inuit and Danish descent. He grew up speaking Greenlandic and is called the father of Eskimology.

In 1910 he founded a trading station at Thule in the far north, which funded seven expeditions. The Fifth Thule Expedition (1921 to 1924) took him by dog sled from Greenland across Arctic Canada to Alaska, the first to cross the Northwest Passage that way.

He recorded the songs, myths and ways of life of many Inuit groups and showed that they shared one language and culture from Greenland to Alaska, the heritage of the Thule migration. He is honoured as a national figure in Greenland.
